title: Vurgu

liveClass.title: Unutulmaz anlar
liveClass.goal: Her öğrenci hayatındaki unutulmaz bir anı devrik yapılarla dramatik bir şekilde anlatır (Never had I felt so..., No sooner had we arrived than..., Little did I know that...). Sınıf en etkileyici cümleleri seçer; ardından aynı anı sade dille anlatarak devrik yapının ne zaman fazla geldiği tartışılır.

lessons.title: Hiç böyle bir şey görmemiştim
lessons.goal: Never, Rarely, Seldom gibi olumsuz zarflarla devrik yapı kurarak bir deneyimi vurgulu anlatabilirim.

discover.title: Bir konuşmadan: Ödül töreni
discover.body:
Thank you all so much. I have to say, never in my life have I felt so honoured.

When I started this project ten years ago, I had no money, no team and no office. Rarely did anyone take us seriously. Seldom have I worked so hard, or doubted myself so much.

But never did I imagine that our small idea would one day reach two million students.

Nor could I have done it without my team. They are the real winners tonight. Rarely do you find people who believe in an idea so completely.

Thank you.

questions.prompt: How did people react to the project at the beginning?
Who does the speaker say are the real winners?

learn.explanation:
**Devrik yapı (inversion)**, olumsuz ya da kısıtlayıcı bir zarf **cümlenin başına** geldiğinde **yardımcı fiil öznenin önüne** geçer. Tıpkı soru cümlesi gibi:

| Normal | Devrik (vurgulu) |
|---|---|
| I have **never** felt so honoured. | **Never have I** felt so honoured. |
| People **rarely** took us seriously. | **Rarely did people** take us seriously. |
| We **seldom** see such talent. | **Seldom do we** see such talent. |
| I had **hardly ever** been abroad. | **Hardly ever had I** been abroad. |

**Yardımcı fiil kuralı:**

- Cümlede yardımcı fiil varsa (have, had, can, will, is) → o fiil öne geçer: *Never **have** I seen ...*
- Yardımcı fiil yoksa (present / past simple) → **do / does / did** eklenir: *Rarely **did** anyone take us seriously.*

**Never before / Never in my life:**

- ***Never before had*** *the city seen such crowds.*
- ***Never in my life have I*** *been so scared.*

**Nor / Neither** (olumsuz ekleme):

- *I didn't see it, **nor did** I hear anything.*

**Üslup:** Devrik yapı **resmî, edebi ya da dramatik** bir etki yaratır: konuşmalar, makaleler, edebiyat. Günlük sohbette fazla kullanmak **yapay** durur.

examples.en: Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
examples.tr: Hiç böyle güzel bir gün batımı görmemiştim.

examples.tr: Şehir nadiren bu kadar yoğun kar görür.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede vurgu genellikle kelime sırasıyla değil, tonlama ve "hiç", "asla" gibi kelimelerle yapılır: "Hayatımda hiç bu kadar onurlandırılmamıştım." İngilizcede bu etki devrik yapıyla sağlanır. Türkçe konuşanların en sık hatası, zarfı başa alıp yardımcı fiili öne almamaktır: "Never I have seen" yanlıştır; "Never have I seen" doğrudur.

lessons.title: Yalnızca değil, -er -mez
lessons.goal: Not only ... but also, No sooner ... than ve Hardly / Scarcely ... when yapılarını doğru zaman ve devrik yapıyla kullanabilirim.

discover.title: Bir romandan: Fırtına
discover.body:
No sooner had we left the harbour than the wind began to rise.

Within minutes, the sky had turned black. Hardly had the captain given the order to turn back when a huge wave crashed over the deck.

Not only did we lose our sails, but the engine also stopped working. For three hours, the little boat was thrown from side to side.

Scarcely had the storm passed when we saw the lights of a fishing boat coming towards us. Not only had they seen our signal, but they had also called the coast guard.

We reached land just before midnight, cold, wet and utterly exhausted, but alive.

questions.prompt: When did the wind begin to rise?
options: Just after they left the harbour
questions.explanation: "No sooner had we left the harbour than the wind began to rise."

questions.prompt: What did the fishing boat do?
options: It saw their signal and called the coast guard.
questions.explanation: "Not only had they seen our signal, but they had also called the coast guard."

learn.explanation:
**1. Not only ... but (also) ...**

| Normal | Devrik |
|---|---|
| We **not only** lost our sails **but also** our engine. | **Not only did we** lose our sails, **but** the engine **also** stopped. |
| She is **not only** talented **but also** hard-working. | **Not only is she** talented, **but** she is **also** hard-working. |

Devrik yapı **sadece "Not only" kısmında** olur; "but" kısmı normal kalır.

**2. No sooner ... than / Hardly ... when / Scarcely ... when** (= -er -mez, tam ... ki)

İki geçmiş olay **hemen arka arkaya** olur. İlk olay **past perfect + devrik**, ikinci olay **past simple**.

| Yapı | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **No sooner had** + özne + V3 + **than** + past simple | **No sooner had** we left **than** it started to rain. |
| **Hardly had** + özne + V3 + **when** + past simple | **Hardly had** I sat down **when** the phone rang. |
| **Scarcely had** + özne + V3 + **when** + past simple | **Scarcely had** she arrived **when** she was asked to leave. |

**Dikkat:** **No sooner** → **than** / **Hardly, Scarcely** → **when**

- ~~No sooner had I arrived when~~ ✗
- ~~Hardly had I arrived than~~ ✗ (bazen duyulur ama standart değil)

**Normal (devrik olmayan) hali de mümkün:** *I had **no sooner** left **than** it started to rain.* / *I had **hardly** sat down **when** ...*

examples.en: No sooner had I paid than I realised I'd forgotten my wallet.
examples.tr: Ödemeyi yapar yapmaz cüzdanımı unuttuğumu fark ettim.

examples.en: Hardly had the film started when the power went off.
Not only did he apologise, but he also offered to pay.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçedeki "-er -mez" yapısı ("eve girer girmez") İngilizcede "No sooner had I entered the house than" ya da "Hardly had I entered the house when" ile karşılanır. Bu yapı Türkçede günlük dildir, ama İngilizcede edebi ve resmîdir; günlük konuşmada "As soon as I got home, ..." daha doğaldır. En sık hata "No sooner ... when" kullanmaktır: "No sooner" her zaman "than" ile eşleşir.

Not only she is clever, but also kind.
Not only is she clever, but she is also kind.

As soon as I got home, he called.

task.prompt: Her şeyin ters gittiği bir günü bir romancı gibi dramatik bir şekilde anlatın. En az bir No sooner ... than, bir Hardly / Scarcely ... when ve iki Not only ... but also yapısı kullanın. Zaman uyumuna (past perfect + past simple) dikkat edin.
task.modelAnswer: It was the worst day of my life. No sooner had I left the house than I realised I'd forgotten my keys. Hardly had I reached the bus stop when the bus drove past without stopping. Not only was I late for my exam, but I had also left my calculator at home. And scarcely had I sat down in the exam room when my phone started ringing. Not only did everyone turn around and stare, but the teacher also asked me to leave!

lessons.title: Ancak o zaman, hiçbir koşulda
lessons.goal: Only after / Only when / Not until ile kısıtlayıcı devrik yapıları ve Under no circumstances / On no account gibi kesin yasakları kullanabilirim.

discover.title: Laboratuvar güvenlik kuralları
discover.body:
SAFETY RULES – PLEASE READ CAREFULLY

Under no circumstances should food or drink be brought into the laboratory.

On no account must chemicals be removed from the building.

Only after receiving full safety training will students be allowed to use the equipment.

Not until the supervisor has checked your work should you leave the lab.

Only in an emergency may the side doors be used.

At no time should students work alone in the lab.

Any student who breaks these rules will be asked to leave immediately.

questions.prompt: When can students use the equipment?
When may the side doors be used?
options: At the end of the day
questions.explanation: "Only in an emergency may the side doors be used."

learn.explanation:
**1. Only + zaman / koşul ifadesi → devrik yapı**

**Dikkat:** Devrik yapı **ana cümlede** olur, "Only" kısmında değil!

| Yapı | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **Only after** + isim / -ing / cümle | **Only after** the meeting **did I** understand. |
| **Only when** + cümle | **Only when** I got home **did I** notice. |
| **Only if** + cümle | **Only if** you work hard **will you** succeed. |
| **Only then** | **Only then did** she realise. |
| **Only by** + -ing | **Only by** working together **can we** solve this. |
| **Only in** + isim | **Only in** an emergency **may** the doors be used. |

**2. Not until** (= ancak ... -ince, ... -e kadar değil)

- *I didn't realise until I got home.* → ***Not until** I got home **did I** realise.*

**3. Kesin yasaklar (çok resmî, kurallar ve uyarılar):**

| Yapı | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **Under no circumstances** | **Under no circumstances should** you open this. |
| **On no account** | **On no account must** the door be left open. |
| **In no way** | **In no way is** this my fault. |
| **At no time** | **At no time did** I feel unsafe. |

**Not:** "No" ile başlayan ifadelerde devrik yapı zorunludur; "Not until" ve "Only" ile başlayan cümlelerde de öyle.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçedeki "ancak ... -ince" yapısı ("ancak eve gelince fark ettim") İngilizcede "Only when I got home did I notice" ya da "Not until I got home did I notice" ile karşılanır. En sık hata, devrik yapıyı yanlış yere koymaktır: "Only when did I get home I noticed" yanlıştır. Devrik yapı her zaman ana cümlede, yani virgülden sonraki kısımdadır.

task.prompt: (1) Bir müze, kütüphane ya da sınav salonu için 4 kuralı resmî bir dille duyurun (Under no circumstances, On no account, Only ... may, At no time). (2) Hayatınızda geç fark ettiğiniz bir şeyi Only when / Only after / Not until ile anlatın.

On no account must visitors touch the paintings. Only in the café may food and drink be consumed. At no time should children be left alone. Now, something I realised too late: only when I started working did I understand how hard my parents had worked. Not until I paid my first rent did I appreciate everything they had done for me.

lessons.title: Hiç bilmiyordum ki
lessons.goal: Little did I know, So ... that, Such ... that devrik yapılarını ve vurgulu do / did yapısını kullanabilirim.

discover.title: Kişisel deneme: Yanlış tren
discover.body:
It was a cold morning in March when I got on the train in Ankara. I was going to Konya. Or so I thought.

Little did I know that I was on a train to Kars, more than twenty hours away.

So tired was I that I fell asleep almost immediately. When I woke up, the landscape outside was covered in snow, and the passengers around me were sharing tea and bread.

Such was their kindness that within an hour I felt like part of the family. An elderly woman did warn me that I was going the wrong way, but by then it was too late to get off.

I did eventually reach Konya, three days late. But I've never regretted that journey. It was the best mistake I've ever made.

questions.prompt: Where was the train actually going?
questions.explanation: "I was on a train to Kars"

questions.prompt: How does the writer feel about the journey now?
options: It was the best mistake they've ever made.
questions.explanation: "It was the best mistake I've ever made."

learn.explanation:
**1. Little did I know / Little did they realise** (= hiç bilmiyordum ki ...)

- *I didn't know at all that ...* → ***Little did I know** that I was on the wrong train.*
- ***Little did she realise** how important that day would be.*

Hikâye anlatımında **merak ve gerilim** yaratmak için çok kullanılır.

**2. So + sıfat / zarf + devrik + that** (= o kadar ... ki)

| Normal | Devrik |
|---|---|
| I was **so tired that** I fell asleep. | **So tired was I that** I fell asleep. |
| He spoke **so quickly that** nobody understood. | **So quickly did he speak that** nobody understood. |

**3. Such + be + isim + that** (= öyle ... idi ki)

| Normal | Devrik |
|---|---|
| Their kindness was **so great that** ... | **Such was their kindness that** ... |
| The noise was so loud that ... | **Such was the noise that** ... |

**4. Vurgulu do / does / did** (olumlu cümlede)

Bir şeyin **gerçekten** olduğunu vurgular, özellikle beklentiye ters düştüğünde ya da itiraz ederken:

- *She **did warn** me.* (Gerçekten uyardı, ben dinlemedim.)
- *I **do like** your idea, but ...* (Gerçekten seviyorum, ama ...)
- ***Do** sit down.* (Lütfen oturun. → çok kibar, resmî davet)

Konuşmada **do / did** vurgulu söylenir.

examples.en: Little did we know that the restaurant was about to close for good.
examples.tr: Restoranın tamamen kapanmak üzere olduğunu hiç bilmiyorduk.

examples.en: So beautiful was the music that several people cried.
examples.tr: Müzik o kadar güzeldi ki birkaç kişi ağladı.

examples.en: I did lock the door. I'm sure I did!

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede "Hiç bilmiyordum ki..." ifadesi, hikâyelerde merak yaratmak için kullanılır ve "Little did I know" ile birebir örtüşür. "O kadar yorgundum ki" ise günlük dilde "I was so tired that" olarak kalabilir; "So tired was I that" daha edebidir. Vurgulu "did" ise Türkçedeki "Ama gerçekten kilitledim!" ya da "Söyledim ya!" tonuna karşılık gelir; olumlu cümlede "did" görünce şaşırmayın.

options: So tired I was that I fell asleep.
So tired was I that I fell asleep.
Such was the noise that we couldn't sleep.
Such the noise was that we couldn't sleep.

task.prompt: Beklenmedik bir şekilde gelişen bir hikâye anlatın (gerçek ya da hayalî). Little did I know ile gerilim yaratın; en az bir So ... that ve bir Such was ... that devrik yapısı kullanın; bir yerde de vurgulu did ile birinin size gerçekten bir şey söylediğini ya da yaptığını vurgulayın.
task.modelAnswer: Five years ago, I applied for a job I didn't really want, just for practice. Little did I know that it would change my life. On the day of the interview, so nervous was I that I spilled coffee on my shirt. But the manager just laughed. Such was her warmth that I immediately relaxed. My friends did tell me to wear a dark shirt, and I should have listened! I got the job, and now that manager is one of my closest friends.

lessons.title: Ölçülü vurgu
lessons.goal: Devrik yapıyı ve diğer vurgu araçlarını bağlama uygun ve ölçülü kullanarak etkileyici bir konuşma metni ya da makale yazabilirim.

discover.title: Mezuniyet konuşması (alıntı)
discover.body:
Dear graduates, dear families, dear teachers,

Four years ago, many of you walked into this building nervous, unsure and, let's be honest, a little lost. Today, you are leaving as confident young adults.

Never have I been prouder of a group of students.

The last four years were not easy. Not only did you have to adapt to online classes during difficult times, but many of you also worked part-time to support your families. Rarely have I seen such determination.

And yet, this is just the beginning. Only by continuing to learn will you keep growing. Only by staying curious will you find work that you love.

You will make mistakes. You will fail sometimes. But under no circumstances should you let failure stop you.

I do believe that each of you has something unique to offer the world. Go and offer it.

Congratulations.

questions.prompt: What extra challenge did many students face?
options: They worked part-time to support their families.
questions.explanation: "many of you also worked part-time to support your families"

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's main message?
options: Keep learning and don't let failure stop you.
questions.explanation: "Only by continuing to learn... under no circumstances should you let failure stop you"

learn.explanation:
**Devrik yapıyı ne zaman kullanmalı?**

| Uygun ✓ | Uygun değil ✗ |
|---|---|
| Resmî konuşmalar, törenler | Arkadaşla sohbet |
| Makaleler, köşe yazıları | Kısa mesajlar |
| Edebi metinler, hikâyeler | Günlük e-postalar |
| Kurallar ve uyarılar | Basit bilgi verme |
| Sınav yazıları (C1 / C2, ölçülü) | Her paragrafta birkaç kez |

**Altın kural: Az ama etkili.** Bir konuşmada ya da makalede **2–4 devrik yapı** yeterlidir. Fazlası yapay ve tekrarlı durur.

**Diğer vurgu araçlarıyla dengeleyin:**

| Araç | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **Üçleme (rule of three)** | *nervous, unsure and a little lost* |
| **Tekrar (anaphora)** | ***Only by** continuing to learn ... **Only by** staying curious ...* |
| **Kısa vurucu cümle** | *Go and offer it.* |
| **Vurgulu do** | *I **do** believe that ...* |
| **Güçlü zarflar** | *utterly, deeply, truly, absolutely* |
| **Doğrudan hitap** | *Dear graduates, ...* |

**Yapı:** Etkileyici bir açılış → bir hikâye ya da örnek → ana mesaj → çağrı (call to action) → kısa kapanış

examples.en: Rarely have I seen such determination.
I do believe that each of you can make a difference.
examples.tr: Her birinizin bir fark yaratabileceğine gerçekten inanıyorum.

examples.en: We came, we learned, we grew.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçe hitabette tekrar ve üçleme çok güçlü bir gelenektir ("Ey Türk gençliği!" gibi). İngilizce hitabette de bu araçlar etkilidir; devrik yapı ise ekstra bir "resmiyet ve dram" katmanı ekler. C1 seviyesinde amaç, bu yapıları bildiğinizi göstermek değil, onları doğru anda ve ölçülü kullanmaktır. Her cümlede devrik yapı kullanan bir metin, hiç kullanmayan bir metinden daha zayıf olabilir.

practice.audioText: Friends, never has our community faced a greater challenge. Not only have prices risen, but many local shops have also closed. But only by working together can we protect the place we call home. So tonight, I ask you: join us.

practice.prompt: Devrik yapıyla yeniden yazın: "We can only succeed by working together." (Only by)

Only by working together can we succeed
Only by working together will we succeed.

task.prompt: Aşağıdakilerden birini yazın (200–250 kelime): (a) Mezun olduğunuz okulun ya da kursunuzun mezuniyet töreni için bir konuşma metni. (b) Bir dergi için "Hayatımı değiştiren an" başlıklı kişisel bir deneme. Ölçülü olarak 3–4 farklı devrik yapı kullanın (Never have I, Not only ... but also, Only by / Only when, Little did I know, So ... that) ve en az iki başka vurgu aracı ekleyin (üçleme, tekrar, vurgulu do, kısa vurucu cümle).
task.modelAnswer:
The moment that changed my life

I was nineteen, sitting on a bench outside a hospital in Izmir, waiting for news about my father. Little did I know that the next three hours would change the way I saw everything.

My father had had a heart attack at work. The doctors were calm, kind and incredibly fast. Not only did they save his life, but they also took the time to explain everything to my mother and me, step by step, in a language we could understand.

Sitting on that bench, I watched them work. They rushed, they listened, they comforted. Never had I seen people do something so important with so much humility.

At the time, I was studying economics, and I didn't enjoy it. Only when I saw those doctors did I realise that I wanted my work to matter to someone.

It wasn't easy. I changed universities, lost two years and had to study harder than ever before. My friends did warn me that it was a crazy decision. Maybe it was.

Today, I'm a nurse in the same hospital. Every time I see a frightened family sitting on that bench, I remember how I felt. And I go and sit with them.

That's all. Just sit with them.

questions.prompt: Bir yerel derginin "Unutamadığım bir yolculuk" köşesi için kişisel bir yazı yazın (200–250 kelime). En az 4 farklı devrik yapı (Never have I / Rarely / Not only ... but also / No sooner ... than / Hardly ... when / Only when / Little did I know / So ... that) kullanın, ama doğal ve ölçülü olsun. En az bir vurgulu do / did ve bir üçleme ekleyin.
questions.modelAnswer:
The journey I will never forget

In the summer of 2019, my best friend and I decided to cycle from Istanbul to Izmir. We had no real training, very little money and a map that was ten years old. Little did we know what we were getting ourselves into.

No sooner had we left the city than it started to pour with rain. By the end of the first day, we were wet, sore and completely lost. Not only had we taken the wrong road, but my friend's bike also had a flat tyre.

The next few days were exhausting. We climbed hills, we slept in tents, we lived on bread and tomatoes. My mother did tell me it was a terrible idea, and there were moments when I agreed with her.

But then something changed. In every village, people stopped to talk to us. They gave us tea, fruit and directions. One family even invited us to stay the night. Rarely have I felt so welcome anywhere.

So beautiful was the coastline near Ayvalık that we stayed there for two extra days.

When we finally arrived in Izmir, eleven days after leaving home, we were thinner, browner and much wiser. Only when I got home and looked at the photos did I realise how much that journey had taught me: about my country, about strangers, and about myself.
